cases.author_key_assessment: Not warranted unconditionally; conditionally defensible for deduplicated value pairs with expected hashing assumptions.

choice_assessments.choice: Hash map storing complements seen so far
choice_assessments.reason: A hash structure can find one match or enumerate distinct value pairs in expected linear processing time under a conventional hashing model. If every matching index pair must be output, total work may be quadratic; the exact stem does not resolve this scope.

The ordinary comparison-sort then scan method is O(n log n) before accounting for output. Listing all matching index pairs can require quadratic output. Do not generalize this to a claim that every conceivable sorting model requires n log n.
The ordinary nested loop checks n(n-1)/2 unordered index pairs, which is quadratic even when few pairs match.

choice_assessments.choice: Binary search for each element's complement
choice_assessments.reason: Ordinary binary search needs sorted searchable data, and one logarithmic search per input does not establish O(n) total work. It also cannot avoid an explicit index-pair output lower bound.

issues: All pairs does not specify index pairs versus deduplicated value pairs.
Find may leave explicit enumeration versus a compressed representation unclear.
The stem states O(n) but does not explicitly say worst-case rather than expected hashing analysis; do not relabel it as an explicit worst-case guarantee.
Empty supported_choices is valid only as no unconditionally warranted choice under unresolved scope, not proof that every conventional interpretation has no answer.
The author explanation is a diagnostic placeholder.
conventional_reading_alternatives: Deduplicated unordered value pairs with expected O(1) hash operations can support the authored algorithm description in expected O(n) time and O(n) auxiliary space.
Explicit index-pair enumeration needs output-sensitive time, at least proportional to n plus the number of returned pairs.

Retaining 1:50,000 ignores the specified resizing if the printed ratio was initially correct. It does not follow from the road data either.
1:100,000 corresponds to halving original lengths from a 1:50,000 basis, not the stated 80% factor. It does not reconcile the measurements.

issues: At a uniform 1:50,000 scale, 5 cm represents 2.5 km, conflicting with the 3 km label for the straight road.
